title: Hermite basis coefficients
statement: For every natural number $n$, every function $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ that belongs to $L^2$ for the product of $n$ standard Gaussian measures, and every multi-index $\alpha:\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\mathbb N$, the coefficient of the $L^2$ class of $f$ at the Hermite Hilbert basis vector indexed by $\alpha$ equals $\int_{\mathbb R^n} f(x)H_\alpha(x)\,d\gamma(x)$, where $H_\alpha$ is the Hermite function and $\gamma$ is that product Gaussian measure.
hypotheses_covered: The function $f$ belongs to $L^2$ for the product of $n$ standard Gaussian measures
